sentences.en: Right now, everybody is waiting to hear what two different sets of judges are going to decide.
sentences.zh: always be is entirely connected into those lands and those waters.

sentences.en: One case in tribal court and one in federal court.
sentences.zh: These lands weren't threatened.

sentences.en: But both of those cases right now hinge entirely on the question of jurisdiction.
sentences.zh: 但目前这两个案件都完全取决于管辖权的问题。

sentences.en: Jurisdiction is a little confusing at different times.
sentences.zh: 管辖权有时会让人感到有些困惑。

sentences.en: And what I try to tell people most of the time, it just means who has the right to decide.
sentences.zh: 我大多数时候试图告诉人们的是，它指的就是谁有权做出决定。

sentences.en: The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources is arguing that the case should not be heard in White Earth tribal court at all,
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州自然资源部辩称，该案根本不应该在白土部落法庭审理，

sentences.en: in part because doing so would apply tribal law to actions taken outside the reservation.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是这样做会将部落法律适用于保护区之外的行为。

sentences.en: And in March, in a move that surprised Frank and Thomas, the White Earth Court of Appeals agreed with that argument.
sentences.zh: 今年三月，白土上诉法院采取了一项令弗兰克和托马斯感到惊讶的举措，同意了这一论点。

sentences.en: Because Line 3 doesn't technically pass through the reservation, they argued that the White Earth band had no say in what went on,
sentences.zh: 因为从技术上讲，3号管线并不穿过保护区，他们认为白土部落对所发生的事情没有发言权，

sentences.en: even if the impact of Line 3 can be seen on the reservation.
sentences.zh: 即使3号管线的影响在保护区内显而易见。

sentences.en: Obviously, Frank disagrees.
sentences.zh: 显然，弗兰克不同意这一点。

sentences.en: He has asked the appeals court to reconsider, and they're now waiting on that decision.
sentences.zh: 他已请求上诉法院重新考虑，他们现在正在等待裁决。

sentences.en: If the appeals courts side with Frank and Thomas, and they get to keep going,
sentences.zh: 如果上诉法院支持弗兰克和托马斯，让他们继续推进，

sentences.en: it's worth considering what would happen next, because the implications would be big.
sentences.zh: 那么值得考虑接下来会发生什么，因为其影响将是巨大的。

sentences.en: Well, first, it's possible that there could be even more appeals that drag on even longer.
sentences.zh: 首先，可能会有更多的上诉导致案件拖延更久。

sentences.en: But if they get through those, then they get to try the case in court officially,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们能挺过这些，那么他们就可以正式在法庭上审理此案，

sentences.en: with arguments and lots more documents filed back and forth.
sentences.zh: 届时会有辩论和更多来回提交的文件。

sentences.en: And if after all of that, they actually win, and the tribal court rules against the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources,
sentences.zh: 如果经过这一切他们真的赢了，且部落法庭做出了对明尼苏达州自然资源部不利的裁决，

sentences.en: then things get really interesting.
sentences.zh: 那么事情就会变得非常有趣了。

sentences.en: And I think that's going to be like gasoline and matches.
sentences.zh: 我认为那将如同火上浇油。

sentences.en: If wild rice prevails in this case, it could mean a few things for both the region and the nation.
sentences.zh: 如果野生稻在此案中胜诉，这对该地区乃至全国都可能意味着几件事。

sentences.en: The most obvious change would be to the local area.
sentences.zh: 最明显的变化将发生在当地。

sentences.en: It would be a blow to the continued use of the Line 3 pipeline,
sentences.zh: 这将打击3号管线的持续使用，

sentences.en: which has been operational since October of last year.
sentences.zh: 该管线自去年十月以来一直处于运营状态。

sentences.en: A court order could, hypothetically, force Enbridge to shut the whole thing down.
sentences.zh: 假设法院的一项命令可能会迫使安桥公司关闭整个管线。

sentences.en: But the reason that Frank and Thomas are both excited about this particular case
sentences.zh: 但弗兰克和托马斯对这个特定案件感到兴奋的原因是，

sentences.en: is because it could change the ways that land is used and developed much more broadly.
sentences.zh: 它可能会更广泛地改变土地的使用和开发方式。

sentences.en: Well, the real question is, what are you trying to protect?
sentences.zh: 真正的关键在于，你试图保护什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'm trying to protect wild rice.
sentences.zh: 我试图保护野生稻。

sentences.en: And by protecting wild rice, wild rice will protect everything else.
sentences.zh: 而通过保护野生稻，野生稻也将保护其他一切。

sentences.en: Like many tribes, the reservation that the White Earth Band currently occupies
sentences.zh: 像许多部落一样，白土部落目前占据的保护区，

sentences.en: is a tiny fraction of the land that their treaty with the United States government actually covers.
sentences.zh: 只是他们与美国政府条约所涵盖土地的一小部分。

sentences.en: Over the years, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 多年来，美国政府

sentences.en: pushed tribal residents onto smaller and smaller plots,
sentences.zh: 将部落居民驱赶到越来越小的地块上，

sentences.en: chipping away at their ancestral homes.
sentences.zh: 不断蚕食他们的祖居地。

sentences.en: But the original treaties often cover vast swaths of land.
sentences.zh: 但最初的条约往往涵盖了大片土地。

sentences.en: And one of the things that Frank and the White Earth Band is asking for in their case
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和白土部落在案件中要求的一件事，

sentences.en: is for a co-permitting agreement for new construction.
sentences.zh: 就是建立一个新的联合许可协议。

sentences.en: In other words, if anybody wants to build something like a pipeline,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果有人想建造像管线这样的东西，

sentences.en: the tribe would have to sign off on it, not just on present-day reservation land,
sentences.zh: 部落必须签字同意，这不仅针对现有的保护区土地，

sentences.en: but for all the land that the original Ojibwe treaties covered.
sentences.zh: 还涵盖了最初奥吉布瓦条约所覆盖的所有土地。

sentences.en: And that is a lot of land.
sentences.zh: 那可是很大一片土地。

sentences.en: We're talking about something like 11 million acres in total.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的总共大约有1100万英亩。

sentences.en: And so the reason why this case has so much potential is that if it's successful,
sentences.zh: 所以这个案件之所以有如此大的潜力，是因为如果它成功了，

sentences.en: it not only validates this kind of tribal rights of nature concept about tribes passing rights of nature laws,
sentences.zh: 它不仅验证了这种部落自然权利的概念，即部落通过自然权利法，

sentences.en: but it also would allow tribes in the United States to reach into all of those treaty lands
sentences.zh: 而且还将允许美国的部落触及所有这些条约土地，

sentences.en: to have control over permits issued on those lands.
sentences.zh: 从而对在这些土地上签发的许可证拥有控制权。

sentences.en: And it doesn't stop at those measly 11 million acres of land.
sentences.zh: 而且它并不止步于那区区1100万英亩土地。

sentences.en: And what Thomas and Frank really hope is that if this case succeeds,
sentences.zh: 托马斯和弗兰克真正希望的是，如果此案成功，

sentences.en: they will be on their way to making the idea of environmental personhood a thing all over the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们将走上让环境人格化理念在美国各地普及的道路。

sentences.en: And that would change laws and save ecosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 那将改变法律并拯救生态系统。

sentences.en: But it might also change something a lot more fundamental.
sentences.zh: 但这可能也会改变一些更根本的东西。

sentences.en: Because in a lot of ways, this idea that nature has rights like a person might
sentences.zh: 因为在很多方面，这种认为自然像人一样拥有权利的理念，

sentences.en: is the complete opposite of a lot of modern economic thinking about nature.
sentences.zh: 与许多现代经济学对自然的看法完全相反。

sentences.en: And I hearken back to Sir Francis Bacon in England who said,
sentences.zh: 我回想起英国的弗朗西斯·培根爵士，他说过，

sentences.en: you know, the job of civilization is to torture nature on a rack to extract your secrets.
sentences.zh: 文明的任务就是把自然放在拷问架上折磨，以榨取其秘密。

sentences.en: Okay, so technically this was a quote from a different fancy pants European scholar.
sentences.zh: 好吧，从技术上讲，这句话出自另一位花哨的欧洲学者。

sentences.en: It was Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz who said this, not Francis Bacon.
sentences.zh: 是戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨说的，而不是弗朗西斯·培根。
zh_words: 戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨

sentences.en: But Leibniz was talking about Bacon when he said it, so...
sentences.zh: 但莱布尼茨说这话时是在谈论培根，所以……

sentences.en: The point is, is that if the concept of the rights of nature really takes off in law,
sentences.zh: 重点是，如果自然权利的概念真的在法律中流行起来，

sentences.en: it means reconsidering more than just one pipeline or one construction project.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要重新考虑的不仅仅是一条管线或一个建设项目。

sentences.en: The whole story needs to change.
sentences.zh: 整个故事需要改变。

sentences.en: The source code needs to change.
sentences.zh: 源代码需要改变。

sentences.en: The DNA needs to be altered.
sentences.zh: DNA需要被重塑。

sentences.en: And the only way that happens is when massive numbers of people begin to move into these institutions
sentences.zh: 而实现这一点的唯一途径是，大量的人开始进入这些机构，

sentences.en: to, in essence, change their DNA.
sentences.zh: 从本质上改变它们的DNA。

sentences.en: That's part of the idea behind rights of nature.
sentences.zh: 这就是自然权利背后的部分理念。

sentences.en: It's not quite there yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没完全实现。

sentences.en: But as a movement, that I think is what it's aiming towards.
sentences.zh: 但作为一场运动，我认为这就是它的目标。

sentences.en: It's changing how everything works.
sentences.zh: 它正在改变一切运作的方式。

sentences.en: And with a shift like that comes some big questions.
sentences.zh: 而随着这种转变，也带来了一些重大问题。

sentences.en: For example, if nature gets the right to live and thrive, like a person might,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果自然像人一样拥有生存和繁荣的权利，

sentences.en: then can you just never build anything again?
sentences.zh: 那么你是否就再也不能建造任何东西了？

sentences.en: Thomas gets this question a lot.
sentences.zh: 托马斯经常遇到这个问题。

sentences.en: He told me that once he was up in New Hampshire trying to convince some skeptics
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，有一次他在新罕布什尔州试图说服一些怀疑论者，

sentences.en: that a couple of local rights of nature laws weren't going to stop development altogether.
sentences.zh: 当地的几项自然权利法并不会完全阻止开发。

sentences.en: Some guy got up in the back and he said,
sentences.zh: 后面有个人站起来说，

sentences.en: well, if we pass this, it means we can't shoot squirrels anymore here in the municipality.
sentences.zh: 如果通过了这个，是不是意味着我们在这个城市就不能再射杀松鼠了？

sentences.en: And so I prepared to answer his question.
sentences.zh: 于是我准备回答他的问题。

sentences.en: But some old guy, his friend got up in the back and he said,
sentences.zh: 但后面有个老头，他的朋友站起来说，

sentences.en: no, Mel, what it means is that we can't shoot all the squirrels.
sentences.zh: 不，梅尔，它的意思是说我们不能把松鼠杀光。

sentences.en: The idea here isn't to actually protect each grain of rice or salmon or squirrel as if it's a human being.
sentences.zh: 这里的理念并不是真的要像保护人类一样保护每一粒稻米、每一条鲑鱼或每一只松鼠。

sentences.en: You can still hunt or fish or build as long as overall it doesn't infringe on the right of the natural system to thrive.
sentences.zh: 只要总体上不侵犯自然系统繁荣的权利，你仍然可以狩猎、捕鱼或建设。

sentences.en: So if a forest is protected, it doesn't mean you can't cut down a tree.
sentences.zh: 所以如果森林受到保护，并不意味着你不能砍树。

sentences.en: It just means you can't cause damage to the ecosystem by taking out so many of the trees that the entire ecosystem folds.
sentences.zh: 它只是意味着你不能通过砍伐过多的树木导致整个生态系统崩溃，从而对生态系统造成损害。

sentences.en: The actual specifics of these debates will always be tricky.
sentences.zh: 这些辩论的具体细节总是很棘手。

sentences.en: Who is to say whether the ocean wants an offshore wind farm that might overall decrease global warming?
sentences.zh: 谁能说海洋是否想要一个可能总体上减少全球变暖的海上风电场？

sentences.en: Who gets to decide if the river would rather have a hydroelectric dam or not?
sentences.zh: 谁来决定河流是更想要一个水电大坝还是不想要？

sentences.en: In other words, who speaks for the trees?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，谁为树木代言？

sentences.en: Other than the Lorax, the answer right now is frustratingly vague in that it depends on the situation.
sentences.zh: 除了罗拉克斯，目前的答案令人沮丧地模糊，因为它取决于具体情况。

sentences.en: In cases of tribal treaties, the indigenous communities would take on that role.
sentences.zh: 在涉及部落条约的案件中，原住民社区将承担这一角色。

sentences.en: But that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非总是如此。

sentences.en: A lawsuit currently awaiting hearing in Florida, for example, has a wetland suing a developer.
sentences.zh: 例如，佛罗里达州目前有一个等待审理的诉讼，是一片湿地在起诉开发商。

sentences.en: There's no treaty involved and no tribe driving the effort.
sentences.zh: 没有涉及条约，也没有部落在推动这项工作。

sentences.en: You want more people, not less, representing ecosystems because you want more of these cases brought, not less.
sentences.zh: 你需要更多的人，而不是更少的人来代表生态系统，因为你希望提起更多的这类案件，而不是更少。

sentences.en: But folks that have some kind of relationship to the ecosystem itself, it's important for those folks to be recognized as guardians or plaintiffs in this case.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些与生态系统本身有某种关系的人来说，让他们被承认为此案的监护人或原告是很重要的。

sentences.en: Extending person-like rights to a non-person is always going to be fraught.
sentences.zh: 将类似人的权利扩展到非人类身上总是充满风险的。

sentences.en: There will always be opportunities for abuse here.
sentences.zh: 这里总会有被滥用的机会。

sentences.en: The process could be hijacked by NIMBYs.
sentences.zh: 这个过程可能会被“邻避主义者”劫持。

sentences.en: We could end up with strange and complicated legal cases that make people scratch their heads and wonder what all these lawyers are doing exactly.
sentences.zh: 我们最终可能会得到一些奇怪而复杂的法律案件，让人们挠头，想知道这些律师到底在做什么。

sentences.en: You know, law itself is a figment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法律本身就是一种虚构。

sentences.en: It's an artificial creation.
sentences.zh: 它是一种人为的创造。

sentences.en: And sure, the rights of nature argument is still a gamble.
sentences.zh: 当然，自然权利的论点仍然是一场赌博。

sentences.en: But for Thomas and Frank, it's worth trying.
sentences.zh: 但对托马斯和弗兰克来说，值得一试。

sentences.en: It's kind of like when you have a pair of glasses on your table and the arm's a little loose and you look over and you've got a pair of scissors on the table and you try to tighten that little screw.
sentences.zh: 这有点像当你桌上有一副眼镜，镜腿有点松，你抬头看到桌上有把剪刀，于是你试着去拧那个小螺丝。

sentences.en: You know, it's not the right tool, but it can work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不是合适的工具，但它能起作用。

sentences.en: Right now, the Manoman case is still up in the air.
sentences.zh: 目前，马诺曼案仍悬而未决。

sentences.en: But Frank is already helping other tribes consider a similar strategy.
sentences.zh: 但弗兰克已经在帮助其他部落考虑类似的策略。

sentences.en: In Seattle, the Sauk-Sue-Yaddle tribe has filed a case in tribal court seeking to protect salmon.
sentences.zh: 在西雅图，索克-苏-亚德尔部落已在部落法庭提起诉讼，寻求保护鲑鱼。

sentences.en: This summer, the rice will grow on the lakes again and the boats will head out the way they always have.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，湖上的稻米将再次生长，船只将像往常一样出发。

sentences.en: Here's Evelyn Bellinger again.
sentences.zh: 再次请出伊芙琳·贝林格。

sentences.en: I was looking back.
sentences.zh: 我当时在回首往事。

sentences.en: I have a picture here of wild rice when they were racing when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我这里有一张我小时候收割野生稻时的照片。

sentences.en: The photo shows a mass of boats and people.
sentences.zh: 照片显示了一大群船只和人群。

sentences.en: Some of the boats are empty, while others are full of bags of rice.
sentences.zh: 有些船是空的，而另一些则装满了稻米袋。

sentences.en: Cars line the road as far as the eye can see.
sentences.zh: 汽车沿着道路排开，一眼望不到头。

sentences.en: They had wooden boats.
sentences.zh: 他们有木船。

sentences.en: It was taken in 1963, so I was about 10 years old.
sentences.zh: 那是1963年拍的，所以我当时大约10岁。

sentences.en: And it was just everybody was so involved with harvesting the rice.
sentences.zh: 每个人都非常投入地收割稻米。

sentences.en: And I remember I could stand outside and I could hear the neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我记得我站在外面能听到邻居们的声音。

sentences.en: You know, they were all getting ready to start racing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都在准备开始收割。

sentences.en: And everybody was happy talking in Ojibwe.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很高兴，用奥吉布瓦语交谈。

sentences.en: Those are some of my best memories.
sentences.zh: 那些是我最美好的回忆。

sentences.en: I guess to me, it was always kind of like connecting with our ancestors, because they've always done this before us.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，这总是像是在与我们的祖先建立联系，因为他们一直在我们之前做这件事。

sentences.en: I just kind of felt that connection.
sentences.zh: 我只是感觉到那种联系。

sentences.en: It's quiet.
sentences.zh: 很安静。

sentences.en: Quiet out there.
sentences.zh: 外面很安静。

sentences.en: And I just, I just always used to get that urge, I want to go.
sentences.zh: 我总是有一种冲动，我想去。

sentences.en: And perhaps by the time Evelyn's grandchildren go out on the lake, the rice will have officially presented its case in court.
sentences.zh: 也许等到伊芙琳的孙辈们去湖上时，稻米已经正式在法庭上陈述了它的诉求。

sentences.en: And when they go out to gather it, they might get to congratulate it on a job well done.
sentences.zh: 当他们去采集它时，他们也许可以祝贺它干得漂亮。

sentences.en: Coming up after the break, we tease out some of the more complicated implications of environmental personhood.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将梳理一些关于环境人格化更复杂的含义。

sentences.en: Like, could a river sue a person?
sentences.zh: 比如，河流可以起诉一个人吗？

sentences.en: And could that person sue a river?
sentences.zh: 那个人可以起诉一条河流吗？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Support for this four-part series exploring the future of health and well-being comes from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation,
sentences.zh: 本系列四集节目探讨健康与福祉的未来，由罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会提供支持，

sentences.en: which is committed to improving health and health equity in the United States.
sentences.zh: 该基金会致力于改善美国的健康状况和健康公平。

sentences.en: Knowing that the healthy, equitable future we all deserve won't simply arrive,
sentences.zh: 深知我们都应得的健康、公平的未来不会自动到来，

sentences.en: RWJF is exploring how new technologies, scientific discoveries, cultural shifts, and unforeseen events,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会正在探索新技术、科学发现、文化转变和不可预见的事件，

sentences.en: like those in today's story, may shape our lives in years to come.
sentences.zh: 比如今天故事中的那些，将如何在未来几年塑造我们的生活。

sentences.en: Through these explorations, they're learning what emerging trends or cutting-edge ideas
sentences.zh: 通过这些探索，他们正在了解哪些新兴趋势或前沿理念，

sentences.en: can help us build a future that provides every individual with a fair and just opportunity to thrive,
sentences.zh: 可以帮助我们建立一个未来，为每个人提供公平公正的繁荣机会，

sentences.en: no matter who they are, where they live, or how much money they have.

sentences.en: So Rose, you make a podcast called Flash Forward, which is all about the future,
sentences.zh: Rose，你制作了一个名为《Flash Forward》的播客，内容全是关于未来的，

sentences.zh: 这意味着你花了很多时间思考未来可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: And we talked about this in the episode about the Manoman case and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们在关于Manoman案的那集里讨论过这个问题，你知道，

sentences.en: how this might impact line three and even environmental policy more generally.
sentences.zh: 这可能会如何影响三号线，甚至更广泛的环境政策。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if this goes any further.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，这是否会走得更远。

sentences.en: I mean, in this future, could I be sued by a river, for example?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在未来，比如我会被一条河流起诉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the short answer to that question is, yes, you, Roman Mars, could hypothetically be sued by a river.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的简短回答是，是的，你，Roman Mars，理论上可能会被一条河流起诉。

sentences.en: If you were, say, dumping stuff into a river that you were not supposed to be,
sentences.zh: 如果你，比如说，往一条你不该往里倾倒东西的河流里倒东西，

sentences.en: and the river's legal representatives decided to bring a case against you,
sentences.zh: 而这条河流的法律代表决定对你提起诉讼，

sentences.en: that is, in fact, a possible future.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个可能的未来。

sentences.en: So Russian River v.
sentences.zh: 所以“俄罗斯河诉Roman Mars案”

sentences.en: Roman Mars is a hypothetically possible future case.
sentences.zh: 是一个理论上可能发生的未来案件。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm trying to think of, like, what this could possibly lead to is, like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在想这最终会导致什么，比如，

sentences.en: do I have to get river insurance or, you know, like, things like that beyond this?
sentences.zh: 除了这些，我是不是还得买河流保险，或者诸如此类的东西？

sentences.en: But let's just assume that me as an individual, A, I wouldn't do that ever.
sentences.zh: 但我们先假设我个人，A，我永远不会那样做。

sentences.en: Just to be clear.
sentences.zh: 先声明一下。

sentences.en: Please believe me.
sentences.zh: 请相信我。

sentences.en: I would just, I would never have flew to a river.
sentences.zh: 我绝对，我绝不会往河里乱扔东西。

sentences.en: But, you know, the damage one person can do to a river, it's pretty limited.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，一个人对河流造成的损害是非常有限的。

sentences.en: Like, we're really talking about industry and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的主要是工业之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, even if you, and I would never besmirch you to suggest this,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使你——我绝不会诋毁你而暗示你会这样做——

sentences.en: but even if you were to throw a wrapper into the river, right,
sentences.zh: 但即使你往河里扔了一个包装纸，对吧，

sentences.en: like, that is not worth the time and resources that would be required to take this to court.
sentences.zh: 那也不值得为此花费时间和资源去法庭起诉。

sentences.en: So I think the likelihood of this being used against singular individuals,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这被用来针对个人的可能性，

sentences.en: you, Roman Mars, me, whatever it is, is very low.
sentences.zh: 针对你，Roman Mars，或者我，无论谁，都非常低。

sentences.en: The point here is to go after big ticket items, you know, pipelines, mining, oil refining, fracking,
sentences.zh: 重点是要针对那些大项目，你知道，管道、采矿、炼油、水力压裂，

sentences.en: all the stuff that you see in the news as kind of like those big players.
sentences.zh: 所有你在新闻里看到的那些大玩家。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, if this legal framework is set up, I could be sued by a river.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果这个法律框架建立起来，我确实可能被河流起诉。

sentences.en: I mean, that's just who gets, you know, chosen to be sued is at the discretion of the people who are suing people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁被选中起诉是由起诉方决定的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And I think it's actually interesting that you picked rivers as the example here
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得很有趣的是，你选择了河流作为例子，

sentences.en: because they are sort of one of the trickier types of environmental cases at play when we talk about rights of nature.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们谈论自然权利时，它们是环境案件中最棘手的一类。

sentences.en: Rivers famously flow, right?
sentences.zh: 河流众所周知是流动的，对吧？

sentences.en: They are often quite long and they often cross state and even national borders.
sentences.zh: 它们通常很长，而且经常跨越州界甚至国界。

sentences.en: And this was Frank's issue with the idea of rights of nature at the beginning as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是Frank一开始对自然权利概念的疑虑。

sentences.en: I was reluctant at first working with Tom on rights of a river because the Mississippi River has probably 30 different water controls associated with the Upper Mississippi River Reservoir System.
sentences.zh: 我起初在和Tom合作研究河流权利时很勉强，因为密西西比河可能与上密西西比河水库系统相关的有30种不同的水控制措施。

sentences.en: Yeah, a river is a complicated entity and it touches a lot of different places and jurisdictions.
sentences.zh: 是的，河流是一个复杂的实体，它触及许多不同的地方和管辖区。

sentences.en: And it makes me wonder, like, OK, if I were to pollute a river up here in Oakland to keep this hypothetical going,
sentences.zh: 这让我很好奇，好吧，如果我为了让这个假设继续下去，在奥克兰污染了一条河，

sentences.en: please understand I would never pollute a river, Rose.
sentences.zh: 请理解，我绝不会污染河流，Rose。

sentences.en: You have to understand.
sentences.zh: 你一定要明白。

sentences.en: I'm just filing this away for a future lawsuit that I'm going to file against you when you pollute a river.
sentences.zh: 我只是把它记下来，留待将来你污染河流时，我要对你提起诉讼。

sentences.en: OK, I would never pollute a river.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我绝不会污染河流。

sentences.en: But if I were to pollute a river in Oakland and the effects of that pollution were felt in, you know, L.A.
sentences.zh: 但如果我在奥克兰污染了一条河，而污染的影响传到了，你知道，洛杉矶，

sentences.en: or San Diego or even Mexico,
sentences.zh: 或者圣地亚哥，甚至墨西哥，

sentences.en: you know, if Mexico had an environmental personhood law, could I be sued by a river like in another country?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果墨西哥有环境人格法，我会被另一个国家的河流起诉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: The true answer is no one knows, right?
sentences.zh: 真实的答案是没人知道，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this has not been a thing that anyone has tried.
sentences.zh: 因为这还没人尝试过。

sentences.en: I think probably you wouldn't be sued by a river from Mexico, at least right now, just because suing somebody from another country opens up a whole other can of worMs.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能不会被墨西哥的河流起诉，至少现在不会，因为起诉另一个国家的人会引发一大堆麻烦。

sentences.en: But if San Diego had an environmental personhood law and they could trace the damage that was done to the river back to you up here in Oakland, then theoretically, yes,
sentences.zh: 但如果圣地亚哥有环境人格法，并且他们能追踪到河流受到的损害源自你这里，在奥克兰，那么理论上，是的，

sentences.en: because you are in the same state.
sentences.zh: 因为你们在同一个州。

sentences.en: It is possible that you could be sued by the river in San Diego.
sentences.zh: 你确实有可能被圣地亚哥的河流起诉。

sentences.en: And I actually asked Thomas Lindsay about this, too, because I'm sort of obsessed with this river question.
sentences.zh: 我其实也问过Thomas Lindsay这个问题，因为我有点沉迷于这个河流问题。

sentences.en: And the answer is, is that these laws have what we refer to as an extra jurisdictional component,
sentences.zh: 答案是，这些法律有所谓的“域外管辖”成分，

sentences.en: which is that if you're recognizing the right of the river to exist,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你承认河流有生存权，

sentences.en: that anything happening upstream from the river that's violating the rights as that river flows through that particular municipality is actionable,
sentences.zh: 那么任何在河流上游发生、且在河流流经该特定城市时侵犯其权利的行为都是可诉的，

sentences.en: which means you can bring a lawsuit against whoever's interfering with the rights by operating upstream.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以对任何通过在上游作业而干扰这些权利的人提起诉讼。

sentences.en: This is a way of applying environmental law in a small place that can have exceptional application outside of that,
sentences.zh: 这是一种在小范围内应用环境法的方法，它可以在此之外产生特殊的应用，

sentences.en: especially when you're dealing with rivers or other ecosystems that, of course, don't respect municipal boundaries.
sentences.zh: 特别是当你处理河流或其他当然不尊重市政边界的生态系统时。

sentences.en: So I part of the reason I like the river example and I think about it all the time is because it does help show something that I got to thinking about a lot when working on this episode,
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢河流这个例子的部分原因，以及我一直思考它的原因，是因为它确实有助于展示我在制作这一集时思考良久的一点，

sentences.en: which is that when you really start to play out some of these future scenarios and you really start to fully buy into this idea and the applications,
sentences.zh: 那就是当你真正开始推演这些未来场景，并真正开始完全接受这个想法及其应用时，

sentences.en: you start to see that this strategy can get a little bit bananas.
sentences.zh: 你会发现这个策略可能会变得有点疯狂。

sentences.en: OK, well, please explain more.
sentences.zh: 好的，请多解释一下。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So there's a case in India that I think kind of illustrates what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 印度有一个案例，我觉得能说明我在说什么。

sentences.en: So in 2017, a court in Uttarakhand granted personhood to the Ganges and Yamuna rivers.
sentences.zh: 2017年，北阿坎德邦的一家法院授予了恒河和亚穆纳河人格权。

sentences.en: Now, the state immediately appealed and ultimately the rivers were stripped of the rights they had just been given before it actually made any difference at all.
sentences.zh: 后来，邦政府立即上诉，最终这些河流被剥夺了刚刚获得的权利，甚至还没产生任何实际影响。

sentences.en: But the thing that is interesting about this is that the issue in this case seemed to not only be about the geographical span of these rivers, right?
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，这个案件的问题似乎不仅在于这些河流的地理跨度，对吧？

sentences.en: They're quite long, but also about what it means to actually say that these rivers are legal persons.
sentences.zh: 它们很长，但也在于说这些河流是“法律人格”到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: So having the rights of a person means being protected from harm, right?
sentences.zh: 拥有人的权利意味着受到保护免受伤害，对吧？

sentences.en: But it also means that you can be held accountable for the harm that you cause.
sentences.zh: 但也意味着你必须为你造成的伤害承担责任。

sentences.en: So you can't punch me and I also can't punch you back.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能打我，我也不能打你。

sentences.en: Speaking of things that we would never do like Palluta River.
sentences.zh: 说到我们绝不会做的事，比如污染河流。

sentences.en: And in this case in India, there actually was a question about whether or not the river could be held accountable for its actions.
sentences.zh: 在印度的这个案例中，确实存在一个关于河流是否能为其行为负责的问题。

sentences.en: So in their appeal, the government asked whether people could sue for any damages that the river caused.
sentences.zh: 所以在上诉中，政府询问人们是否可以就河流造成的任何损害提起诉讼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK, so like if the river flooded and destroyed my house, you know, it could theoretically be responsible if it was a person.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以如果河流泛滥摧毁了我的房子，你知道，如果它是一个人，理论上它可能要负责。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this was a concern that was cited in the appeal by the government saying, like, we can't open this can of worms because, like, what happens if people sue the river back?
sentences.zh: 这也是政府在上诉中提到的担忧，他们说，我们不能打开这个潘多拉魔盒，因为如果人们反过来起诉河流怎么办？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because, like, how do you hold a river accountable?
sentences.zh: 因为，你该怎么让一条河流负责呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I genuinely don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: And I think it would probably involve the state just having to pay for it, right, if the state is representing the river.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能意味着国家必须为此买单，对吧，如果国家代表这条河流的话。

sentences.en: But, like, again, no one knows what that would look like.
sentences.zh: 但同样，没人知道那会是什么样子。

sentences.en: So I will say advocates for environmental personhood say that they're not really actually arguing that rivers should be treated exactly like people.
sentences.zh: 所以我得说，环境人格的倡导者们表示，他们并不是真的在争论河流应该被完全像人一样对待。

sentences.en: I think they all kind of recognize that that way madness lies.
sentences.zh: 我想他们都意识到那条路是通往疯狂的。

sentences.en: But sometimes they will use the term legal naturehood instead of legal personhood, which is, you know, legal people love to coin new words for things.
sentences.zh: 但有时他们会使用“法律自然权”而不是“法律人格”这个词，你知道，法律界人士喜欢为事物创造新词。

sentences.en: I don't know what that means necessarily.
sentences.zh: 我不一定知道那意味着什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It still opens up this question of, like, which rights nature does get and which ones it doesn't get.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然引出了一个问题，即自然界到底获得了哪些权利，又没获得哪些权利。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But giving it a new name at least sort of sidesteps the asymmetry of the term personhood.
sentences.zh: 但给它一个新名字至少在某种程度上避开了“人格”一词的不对称性。

sentences.en: But it's still sort of a confounding thought exercise.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然是一个令人困惑的思想实验。

sentences.en: Like, again, like when we talked about polluting the river in Oakland, again, something we would never do.
sentences.zh: 就像我们之前说的在奥克兰污染河流一样，再次声明，我们绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: So and it reaching San Diego to cause harm, you know, historically, San Diego has always had the right to sue somebody upriver for causing harm.
sentences.zh: 如果它蔓延到圣地亚哥造成损害，你知道，历史上，圣地亚哥一直有权起诉上游造成损害的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, why do we need a new law when you do have these other enforcement mechanisms already?
sentences.zh: 既然已经有了这些执法机制，为什么还需要新法律呢？

sentences.en: You know, I am not a lawyer, but I think that what Frank and Thomas would argue is that, yeah, we have all of these ways of suing, but none of them work to protect the river.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是律师，但我认为Frank和Thomas会争辩说，是的，我们有所有这些起诉方式，但没有一种能真正保护河流。

sentences.en: And so why not try this other way?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么不试试这种新方法呢？

sentences.en: And, like, I will be honest that to me, philosophically, the idea of environmental personhood, of rights of nature, it does appeal to me.
sentences.zh: 而且，老实说，从哲学上讲，环境人格、自然权利的想法确实吸引我。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like this idea that we should respect these places.
sentences.zh: 就像我们应该尊重这些地方的想法一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That they're living entities, that we should think about them as truly alive.
sentences.zh: 它们是活生生的实体，我们应该把它们视为真正有生命的。

sentences.en: I also buy into the idea that the current environmental regulations are not working.
sentences.zh: 我也认同目前的环保法规行不通的观点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That the system we have is not working.
sentences.zh: 我们现有的系统行不通。

sentences.en: But at the same time, when you start to look into these specific examples, right, like, can the river sue you back?
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，当你开始研究这些具体案例时，对吧，比如，河流能反过来起诉你吗？

sentences.en: Like, what does this really mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: I can't help but feeling like we're sort of trying to force a square peg into a round hole of sort of an indigenous thought system into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我不禁觉得我们是在试图把方钉强行塞进圆孔里，把某种原住民思想体系塞进美国的法律体系中。

sentences.en: legal system.
sentences.zh: 而这两者从根本上来说并不是一回事。

sentences.en: And those are just kind of not fundamentally the same things.
sentences.zh: 我确实问过Thomas这个问题。

sentences.en: And I did ask Thomas about this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们讨论了很多。

sentences.en: We talked about it a lot, actually.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次问他时，他基本上说，是的，显然那里有两种不同的世界观，一种已被证明具有极大的破坏性，

sentences.en: And when I first asked him, he was basically like, yeah, like, obviously there's two different worldviews there, one which has proven to be incredibly destructive,
sentences.zh: 几乎是世界性的、全球性的破坏。

sentences.en: almost world destructive, globally destructive.
sentences.zh: 而另一种以完全不同的眼光看待自然，认为人类需要与自然和谐共处，而不是试图爬到它头上，把它绑在架子上，用中世纪的刑具折磨它。

sentences.en: And another one that sees nature in a much different light in which humans need to live in some kind of harmony or compatibility with nature rather than trying to climb on top of it and stretch it on a rack and torture it in a medieval torture device.
sentences.zh: Thomas确实很喜欢关于刑具的那句名言，我也很喜欢。

sentences.en: Thomas does love that quote about the torture device, which I also love.
sentences.zh: 他说话从不拐弯抹角。

sentences.en: He doesn't mince words.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他。

sentences.en: I like him.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 而且，也许这没关系，对吧？

sentences.en: And, like, maybe that's fine, right?
sentences.zh: 也许如果我们能取得成果，我们是否在试图把方钉塞进圆孔里并不重要，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe it doesn't matter if we are trying to force this square peg into a round hole if it gets results, right?
sentences.zh: 考虑到目前的环境状况，我们并没有大量的时间坐在这里完美地完成这件事。

sentences.en: Like, it's not as though we just have a ton of time to sit around and do this perfectly, given the state of the environment right now.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一种策略，迫使我们为了结果而接受法律的荒谬性。

sentences.en: But it is sort of a strategy that really pushes us to kind of be, I think, okay with the absurdity of the law in the name of an outcome.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是Frank在那篇文章中提到的关于法律有多愚蠢的内容。

sentences.en: I mean, this was kind of what Frank was getting at in the piece about how dumb law can be.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 因为你确实可以用各种不同的方式来利用它。

sentences.en: Because you really can use it in all kinds of different ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是相互冲突的逻辑论证，你可以整天进行逻辑辩论而永远没有终点。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is conflicting logic arguments, and you can have logic arguments all day long and never be done.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，现在，自然法律运作的那种奇怪而愚蠢的方式，有利于那些通常在污染的人。

sentences.en: And, like, right now, the weird and silly way that nature laws work, work in favor of people who are generally polluting.
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么不反其道而行之呢？

sentences.en: So, like, why not do it the opposite way?
sentences.zh: 为什么不让它有利于自然呢？

sentences.en: Why not make it work in favor of nature?
sentences.zh: 完全合理。

sentences.en: Totally fair.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，Frank和Thomas看到了这个差距，他们确实在努力让某些事情现在就发挥作用，同时也着眼于大局。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, Frank and Thomas see this gap, and they are really trying to make something work now while also thinking bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以两者兼顾，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you can do both, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以做你那些奇怪的小法律修补，同时也试图构想一个更全面的系统。

sentences.en: You can do your, like, weird little law fiddling and also be trying to imagine a system that is a little bit more holistic.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一场彻底的改革。

sentences.en: What we're talking about is a complete overhaul here.
sentences.zh: 这只是以不同方式看待世界的开始，因为在西方法律体系中，没有比“自然是财产”更根深蒂固的概念了。

sentences.en: This is just the beginning of seeing the world in a different way, because if there's no better,
sentences.zh: 它基本上是西方文化或西方文明中一切事物的基石。

sentences.en: well-trod concept in the Western system of law than the one in which nature is property.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's basically the building block for everything in a Western culture or Western civilization.
sentences.zh: 而他谈论的是自然不再是财产。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's talking about nature not being property.
sentences.zh: 而且他谈论的是自然不再是财产。

sentences.en: So, it's just a complete overhaul of Western civilization as we know it.
sentences.zh: 所以，这简直是对我们所知的西方文明的一次彻底重构。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, like, I'll just pencil it in.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我先把它记在日程表上吧。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm probably free Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我周三应该有空。

sentences.en: I don't know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你在忙什么。

sentences.en: You know, we'll just work on it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们会一起研究的。

sentences.en: We'll just knock it out on a Zoom.
sentences.zh: 我们开个Zoom会议把它搞定就行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Really, really epic Zoom.
sentences.zh: 一场非常、非常史诗级的Zoom会议。

sentences.en: But, like, in all seriousness, I actually think that is why I got really interested in this idea in the first place and, like,
sentences.zh: 但说真的，我确实认为这就是我最初对这个想法产生浓厚兴趣的原因，而且，

sentences.en: why I wanted to explore these cases and I think why we keep talking about this, right?
sentences.zh: 也是我想要探索这些案例的原因，我想这也是我们一直讨论这个话题的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: I spend a lot of time on Flash Forward, my podcast, thinking about what might move us to a better future.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间在我的播客《Flash Forward》上，思考什么能推动我们走向更美好的未来。

sentences.en: And when you look at history, as you do on this show all the time, and there's lots of episodes that you can point to that talk about this kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 当你审视历史时——就像你们在这个节目里经常做的那样，有很多集节目都可以指出这一点——

sentences.en: you realize that often it's these, like,
sentences.zh: 你会意识到，往往正是这些，比如，

sentences.en: weird little strategies that no one is expecting that kind of make a huge difference because they come out of left field and do ask people to think about the world differently.
sentences.zh: 那些没人预料到的奇怪小策略，反而产生了巨大的影响，因为它们出其不意，要求人们以不同的方式思考世界。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So if a river being able to sue you, Roman, for your pollution that you will never do, if that's what gets us to, like, a better place and saving the environment, I'm for it,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果让河流有权起诉你——罗曼，虽然你永远不会去污染它——如果这就是能让我们走向更美好的未来并拯救环境的方法，我支持，

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, it's really fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是非常迷人的内容。

sentences.en: I've loved watching this story come together.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到这个故事一点点成形。

sentences.en: It's so much fun to think about.
sentences.zh: 思考这些问题真的很有趣。

sentences.en: So thank you so much for bringing it to us and doing this with us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你把它带给我们，并和我们一起完成这期节目。

sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks.
